method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, constructor-by-constructor replay of both recursive definitions, verification of the two propositions and exercises, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Immediate, proper and general subformulas; recursive well-definedness; transitivity and the subformula-count bound.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A formula is one of its own subformulas, while every other subformula is proper.
samples.checks: The inclusive meaning of subformula and strict meaning of proper subformula are both retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Atomic formulas have no immediate subformulas; a unary or quantified formula has its body as the sole immediate subformula, and a binary formula has its two operands.
samples.checks: The atomic, negation, binary-connective, universal and existential cases agree exactly with the source constructors.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Proper subformulas are defined recursively: each immediate constituent and all of that constituent's proper subformulas are included; all subformulas add the formula itself.
samples.checks: Every recursive clause preserves which constituents and descendants are included, and the general definition adds exactly the root formula.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The immediate definition is explicit by cases, whereas the proper-subformula definition calls itself only on smaller, earlier formulas, which makes the recursion well defined.
samples.checks: The explicit-versus-recursive contrast, inductive-set context, function language and earlier-argument restriction are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The subformula relation is transitive, and a formula containing n connectives and quantifiers has at most 2n+1 subformulas; each assertion is followed by a proof exercise.
samples.checks: Both hypotheses, the transitive conclusion, the exact bound and both internal references are preserved.

source_observations: The translation consistently distinguishes immediate, proper and inclusive subformula relations.
The recursive clauses are checked as structural clauses rather than summarized informally.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi subformula term family is evidence-backed but remains explicitly open to specialist review in T213.
